original.target_description: Timing of OQ-45 NOT progress alerts in group therapy versus the archival individual no-feedback condition; preliminary comparison F(1, 443) = 61.84.

n.location: p. 125 (PDF p. 10), Exploratory Analysis of NOT OQ-45 Cases With Archival No-Feedback Condition; canonical L691–L707, particularly L698–L703
n.quote: We retrieved data from 318 patients who signaled as ... NOT from four of the six studies summarized by Shimokawa ... We then identified NOT OQ-45 cases in ... our study, locating 59 patients in the GQ ⫹ OQ-45 condition and ... 67 patients in the OQ-45 control condition.
n.sample_role: Analytic participants selected for at least one NOT OQ-45 alert: 318 archival individual patients, 59 GQ/OQ-45 group patients, 67 OQ-45-only group patients.
n.exclusions: Archival patients selected from individual no-feedback therapy with NOT alerts, from four of six studies; current trial patients selected for NOT OQ-45 alerts in two mutually exclusive randomized arms. Additional timing-specific missingness not stated. Later exclusion of 15 efficacy cases belongs to a different outcome analysis.

replication.target_description: Timing of first NOT alert among UCC clients who alerted at least once, group versus individual therapy, F(1, 1258) = 3.55. This matches the neutral timing description, but supplied Table 1 is the frequency outcome; the timing test is Table 2.

n.sample_role: Clients with at least one NOT alert in mutually exclusive individual-only (1,214) and group-only (46) samples, contributing first-alert timing.
n.exclusions: Valid OQ-45 administrations with more than two data points; individual/group therapy only; other treatment types excluded; first episode only (90-day gap defines new episode); concurrent group/individual therapy excluded; alerts examined during Sessions 2–15. Timing additionally excludes never-alerting clients.
n.quote: Figure 3. Comparing the percentages of ﬁrst-time, not-on-track alerts by session between ... individual (N!1,214) and group (N!46) treatment for the present study.

notes:
Requested OR is not printed for the timing comparison in either paper. F statistics are retained as printed, with no conversion. Supplied replication Table 1 refers to NOT alert rates, not timing; target_match=false records this known locator mismatch, while the actual timing comparison is separately identified and extracted from the prose/Table 2. Authors explicitly state nonreplication of first-alert timing, while noting low power (.27) and uncertainty about format differences. Source is the author-uploaded replication paper and a full HTML copy of the original paper; titles and DOI strings verified. ResearchGate HTML renders equals signs as !. n quote fields contain compact noncontiguous numeric excerpts from the cited caption.
